([[Macomb Township, Michigan]]) | college = [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] (2020–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 44 | draft_team = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2022|full=y}} | team1 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team2 = →[[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | years3 = {{nbay|2023|full=y}} | team3 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years4 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team4 = →[[Capital City Go-Go]] | years5 = {{nbay|2023|end}}–present | team5 = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | years6 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team6 = →[[Wisconsin Herd]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA Cup champions|NBA Cup champion]] ([[2024 NBA Cup|2024]]) * First-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] (2022) * MAC Freshman of the Year (2021) * MAC All-Freshman Team (2021) }} '''Ryan Anthony Rollins''' (born July 3, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo Rockets]]. ==Early life== Rollins was born and raised in [[Detroit]], Michigan.{{cite web |last=Murray |first=Derek |title=2022 NBA Draft Q&A: Toledo's Ryan Rollins is 'the guy you want' |url=https://www.basketballnews.com/stories/2022-nba-draft-qa-toledos-ryan-rollins |publisher=Basketball News |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=May 26, 2022}} He played basketball for [[Dakota High School (Michigan)|Dakota High School]] in [[Macomb Township, Michigan]]. As a junior, he averaged 17.1 points, seven rebounds, 3.2 assists and 2.5 steals per game, missing the second half of the season with a hamstring injury.{{cite web |last=Purcell |first=Jared |title=Dakota's Ryan Rollins more concerned with playoff run than Mr. Basketball |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2020/02/dakotas-ryan-rollins-more-concerned-with-playoff-run-than-mr-basketball.html |publisher=MLive |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=February 5, 2020}} In his senior season, Rollins averaged 25.5 points, nine rebounds and five assists per game, earning second-team All-State honors from the [[Associated Press]]. A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] after the program prioritized him early in the recruiting process.{{cite web |last=Buckey |first=Brian |title=Incoming point guard Rollins ready to learn the ropes at Toledo |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2020/06/04/incoming-point-guard-ryan-rollins-ready-to-learn-the-ropes-at-toledo/stories/20200604091 |website=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=June 4, 2020}} ==College career== Rollins immediately made an impact as a freshman at Toledo.{{cite web |last=Rowland |first=Kyle |title=UT freshman Rollins plays like a veteran |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2021/03/08/UT-freshman-Rollins-plays-like-a-veteran/stories/20210308022 |website=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=March 8, 2021}} He averaged 13.7 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, and was named [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC) Freshman of the Year after helping his team win the MAC regular season title.{{cite web |last=Rowland |first=Kyle |title=UT's Rollins will keep name in NBA draft |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2022/05/31/ut-s-rollins-will-keep-name-in-nba-draft/stories/20220531137 |website=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=May 31, 2022}} Rollins assumed a leading role in his sophomore season with the transfer of [[Marreon Jackson]].{{cite web |last=Sansom |first=Jordan |title=Toledo Rockets star Ryan Rollins looks to take the next step in his game |url=https://bvmsports.com/2021/12/13/toledo-rockets-star-ryan-rollins-looks-to-take-the-next-step-in-his-game/ |publisher=BVM Sports |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=December 13, 2021}} On November 24, 2021, he scored a career-high 35 points in a 79–70 victory over [[Coastal Carolina Chanticleers men's basketball|Coastal Carolina]] to win the [[Nassau Championship]], where he was named tournament [[most valuable player]].{{cite web |last=French |first=Simba |title=Rockets wins inaugural 'Nassau Championship' |url=https://thenassauguardian.com/rockets-wins-inaugural-nassau-championship/ |website=[[The Nassau Guardian]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=November 26, 2021}} Rollins helped Toledo repeat as MAC regular season champions.{{cite web |title=Toledo Claims Share of MAC Regular Season Title |url=https://getsomemaction.com/news/2022/3/1/mens-basketball-toledo-claims-share-of-mac-regular-season-title.aspx |publisher=[[Mid-American Conference]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=March 1, 2022}} As a sophomore, he averaged 18.9 points, six rebounds and 3.6 assists per game, earning first-team All-MAC honors. On April 7, 2022, Rollins declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility. He opted to remain in the draft, forgoing his remaining college eligibility. == Professional career == === Golden State Warriors (2022–2023) === In the [[2022 NBA draft]], Rollins was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 44th overall pick. He was later traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Tyrese Martin]], the 51st pick in the draft, and cash considerations.{{Cite web |title=Warriors Acquire Draft Rights To Ryan Rollins From Atlanta Hawks |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/draft-rights-ryan-rollins-20220623 |access-date=2022-09-03 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} On July 28, 2022, Rollins signed his rookie contract with the Warriors.{{Cite web |title=Warriors Sign Ryan Rollins |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-ryan-rollins-20220728 |access-date=2022-09-03 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} He did not play for the Warriors in the [[NBA Summer League]] due to a right foot injury.{{Cite web |title=Ryan Rollins Injury Update – 6/29/22 |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/ryan-rollins-injury-update-20220629 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=Golden State Warriors}} On February 6, 2023, the Warriors announced that Rollins would undergo season-ending surgery to repair a [[Jones fracture]] of the fifth metatarsal in his right foot.{{Cite web |title=Warriors PR on Twitter: "Warriors guard Ryan Rollins to undergo surgery" |url=https://twitter.com/WarriorsPR/status/1622667440277823490 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=Twitter}} ===Washington Wizards (2023–2024)=== On July 6, 2023, Rollins was traded, alongside [[Jordan Poole]], [[Patrick Baldwin Jr.]] and draft picks, to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Chris Paul]].{{cite web|title=Wizards acquire Poole, Baldwin Jr. and Rollins along with a First and Second Round Pick in trade with Warriors|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-acquire-poole-baldwin-jr-and-rollins-along-with-a-first-and-second-round-pick-in-trade-with-warriors|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 6, 2023}} However, he was waived on January 8, 2024.{{cite web|title=Wizards Waive Ryan Rollins|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-waive-ryan-rollins|website=NBA.com|date=January 8, 2024|access-date=January 9, 2024}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2024–present)=== On February 21, 2024, Rollins signed a two–year, [[two-way contract]] with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Ryan Rollins to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-ryan-rollins-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2024|access-date=February 22, 2024}} He would make three appearances for Milwaukee during the remainder of the year. On March 4, 2025, the Bucks converted Rollins' two-way contract into a standard NBA contract.{{cite web | title=Milwaukee Bucks Convert Ryan Rollins to Standard NBA Contract | website=NBA | date=2025-03-04 | url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-convert-ryan-rollins-to-standard-nba-contract | access-date=2025-12-06}} He made 53 appearances (19 starts) for Milwaukee during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 6.2 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists. On July 8, 2025, Rollins signed a three-year, $12 million contract to return to the Bucks.{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Re-Sign Ryan Rollins|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-re-sign-ryan-rollins|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2025|access-date=July 9, 2025}}{{cite tweet|first=Shams|last=Charania|title=Free agent guard Ryan Rollins has agreed to a three-year, $12 million deal to return to the Milwaukee Bucks, with a player option in the third season, agents Mike Silverman and Brandon Grier of Equity Sports tell ESPN.|number=1942046311932481643|user=ShamsCharania|date=July 6, 2025|access-date=July 9, 2025}} Entering the 2025–26 season, he was named the starting point guard after the team waived [[Damian Lillard]]. On October 30, Rollins put up a career-high 32 points in a 120–110 win over the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/milwaukee-bucks/bucks-news-ryan-rollins-message-revenge-game-warriors|title=Bucks guard Ryan Rollins' immediate message after wild revenge game vs. Christopher played [[college basketball]] for [[Davenport Panthers|Davenport]].{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Jim |title=A little R&R: Dakota hoops star Ryan Rollins signs with Toledo |url=https://www.macombdaily.com/2019/11/18/a-little-rr-dakota-hoops-star-ryan-rollins-signs-with-toledo/ |website=[[The Macomb Daily]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=November 18, 2019}} On January 12, 2024, Rollins was charged with seven counts of petty [[larceny]] after being caught shoplifting household items from a local [[Target Corporation|Target]] store on seven occasions.{{Cite web |last=Helin |first=Kurt |date=2024-01-12 |title=Former Wizards guard Ryan Rollins charged with shoplifting from Target multiple times while with team |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/former-wizards-guard-ryan-rollins-charged-with-shoplifting-from-target-multiple-times-while-with-team |access-date=2024-03-03 |website=[[NBC Sports]] |language=en}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{basketballstats|nba=1631157|bbr=r/rolliry01}} *[https://utrockets.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ryan-rollins/7490 Toledo Rockets bio] {{Milwaukee Bucks current roster}} {{navboxes|list= {{2022 NBA draft}} {{Milwaukee Bucks 2024 NBA Cup champions}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Rollins, Ryan}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Atlanta Hawks draft picks]] [[Category:Basketball players from Detroit]] [[Category:Capital City Go-Go players]] [[Category:Golden State Warriors players]] [[Category:Milwaukee Bucks players]] [[Category:Santa Cruz Warriors players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Toledo Rockets men's basketball players]] [[Category:Washington Wizards players]] [[Category:Wisconsin Herd players]]
